meta: Anthropic and OpenAI both split their models into tiers with names that sound like poetry. This video compares them to choosing a scooter, a car, a truck or a big rig: no model is best, only best for the job.

muc.title: Names that sound like poetry
muc.text: Haiku, Sonnet, Opus, Fable. Luna, Sol, Astra. One company, a whole lineup of models. Which one should you pick?

muc.title: Like a scooter, a car and a truck
muc.text: Think of it like choosing a vehicle. The same company makes scooters, cars and trucks. No vehicle is "the best", only the right one for the job.

muc.title: Fast and cheap
muc.text: Small models like Anthropic's Haiku or OpenAI's Luna answer fast and cost very little. They suit simple tasks done in large amounts.

muc.title: Balanced
muc.text: Middle models like Sonnet or Sol balance quality, speed and price. They're the default choice for most everyday work.

muc.title: Very powerful
muc.text: Large models like Opus or Astra reason deeply and handle hard tasks, but they're slower and much more expensive.

muc.title: Anthropic's Fable
muc.text: Fable is the top tier Anthropic added in mid-2026, above even Opus. It's made for very long, very hard work, like letting an AI agent run a whole project for hours. It's also the most expensive tier.

muc.title: The real price gap
muc.text: The gap is big. With OpenAI, the largest tier costs about a hundred times more than the smallest for the same amount of text.

muc.title: Start with the middle tier
muc.text: Start with a middle-tier model. If it's not good enough, move up to a large one. Only very long, hard work needs Fable. For simple, repeated tasks, go down to a small one for speed and low cost.
